title: Layer-Specific Hardware Pooling Designs for CNN Accelerators
problem: CNN accelerator design typically uses uniform pooling (e.g., max pooling only), but different layers may benefit from different pooling strategies.
motivation: Optimization of hardware efficiency and model accuracy by tailoring pooling strategy to individual layers; explore combinatorial approaches beyond single pooling method.
method: The team tested many combinations of pooling methods—techniques that reduce the amount of data in neural networks while preserving important information—across different layers of three real neural networks: AlexNet, UNet, and VGG-16. They combined max pooling (which keeps the largest value in each region) with deviation-based methods such as AAD, BWAD, and AMD (which keep values that stand out significantly from the average). They then built this design twice: once as an FPGA (field-programmable gate array—reconfigurable hardware) on a Xilinx Zedboard, and once as a custom integrated circuit using Cadence tools at 45-nanometer scale.
key_novelty: Using different pooling methods—mixing max pooling with deviation-based techniques—tailored to each layer of a neural network accelerator outperforms applying the same pooling method throughout.
contributions: Improved model accuracy with hardware gains
For AlexNet with pattern '110' (BWAD-BWAD-Max): 4.27% footprint saving vs Max, 14.77% vs AAD, 11.87% vs BWAD, 14.64% vs AMD
limitations: Abstract only; limited to three CNN architectures; no power consumption data; no inference latency analysis; applicability to modern architectures (ResNet, MobileNet) unclear.
